## Correction to the preceding comment: there is NO within-file drift

The previous comment reports that `_cli/help/transition.txt` is 11 lines, that its usage line omits
both `--caused-by` and `--ref`, and that `--ref` is nonetheless described in the body — concluding
the file has drifted against itself and that the fix must therefore cover three drifts rather than
one.

**Checked against `origin/main`; that is not the case.**

```
lines: 22
line  1: Usage: rebar transition [--output {text,json}] [--reason REASON]
line  3:                         [--ref REF] [--force [FORCE]]
line 21:   --ref REF             verify/sign the completion gate against this ref
```

The usage block **wraps across lines 1-3**. `--ref` appears in it (line 3) and is described in the
body (line 21) — consistent, not drifted. Reading only line 1 and treating it as the whole usage
string is what produced the discrepancy.

`--caused-by` is absent from this file **entirely** — not from the usage while present in the body,
but from both. So the defect is exactly what this ticket originally described: a single cross-file
drift between `_cli/help/transition.txt` and the help blob at `_commands/transition.py:65`,
introduced when `0f999860ad` added the flag and updated only the latter.

### The proposed remedy still stands, on its own merits

The suggestion to validate the rendered help against `build_transition` — the parser being the real
authority — with a test asserting every parser-registered flag appears in the rendered help, is
sound and worth keeping. It just is not motivated by a third drift that does not exist.

That requirement is already this ticket's third acceptance criterion, which asks for a test
'derived from the parser rather than a hand-written list'. No AC change is needed.

Recording this so a future implementer does not go looking for a within-file inconsistency and
conclude the file was fixed out from under them.
